scope: Own and stop the terminal input reader before editor, suspend/resume and shell handoffs. Bound asynchronous stop and fail closed on an unhealthy reader; never join from Drop. An active editor retains custody across SIGCONT.

resolved_findings.evidence: input.rs:57-74 cancels, closes the queue, asynchronously waits at most one second for is_finished, and joins only a finished worker. input.rs:84-89 never joins in Drop. Timeout consumes/detaches the ordinary std thread handle, avoiding an unbounded Tokio blocking-pool task. Each handoff propagates stop failure before spawning an editor, stopping the process, or creating another reader. Outer cleanup still restores the terminal on failure.
chat/code.rs:467-472 leaves events absent and the view suspended after CONT while editing. Reader creation and mode resumption occur when the editor job completes at 430-433.

agent_sessions.rs:1080-1083 stops input before view.finish and lease cleanup on all inner-loop results. Chat does the equivalent at 180-185. Native wraps the fallible loop and stops at 362 before NativeView's destructor restores modes.

code_tui_pty.rs:2037-2044 inspects only the composer suffix after the final Message heading. Earlier committed transcript text cannot satisfy that predicate. The interactive second round includes TSTP/CONT while the editor owns input.

performed: Inspected updated diff, new reader implementation/tests, every reader stop/restart site, error exits, and native view destructor.
Read the supplied hang sample: old TerminalInput::Drop is waiting in join while the reader remains inside crossterm Unix mio try_read/read.
verification.not_performed: No Cargo, tests, process control, network comments, or source edits. Parent is running the revised terminal and unit selection.
verification.dependency: Direct locked crossterm 0.28.1; the backend EOF bug remains upstream but no longer forces an unbounded join in these callers.

nonblocking_notes.text: The stuck-worker test exercises refusal/timeout and catches an unconditional join regression. For a stronger runtime-liveness assertion, optionally run a concurrent timer/heartbeat and assert it advances before stop completes; an outer Tokio timeout alone cannot preempt a synchronously blocking future.
Checklist-only style notes remain: new tests follow repository naming rather than ut_/sdv_ prefixes and lack the checklist's formal UT/SDV descriptions. These do not block approval.

residual_limits: A backend-stuck OS reader may remain detached until process exit. Successful terminal handoff requires a finished worker; timeout exits the UI path without launching a competing reader.
Static review does not establish Windows runtime behavior or passing test results.

implementation_review.evidence: stop takes ownership, sets cancellation and closes the bounded channel before asynchronously checking worker completion under a one-second timeout. It joins only after is_finished. Drop cancels without joining, and the timeout drops an ordinary OS-thread handle rather than occupying a Tokio blocking-pool worker. Handoff callers propagate failure before an editor is polled or a replacement reader is created.

SIGCONT resumes the view and input only when no editor is active. While editing, events remain absent and modes remain suspended until the editor job completes. The editor future is lazy and first polled after reader stop and view suspension.

Normal and fallible loop results pass through explicit reader stop before terminal cleanup. Chat and agent deck restore modes before lease cleanup. Native wraps the fallible loop so stop executes before NativeView drops. Reader creation errors retain view destructor cleanup.

Both editor modes exercise three round trips and verify three exact Unicode/multiline prompt payloads. The interactive fixture consumes a required input line, suspends/continues in round two, and waits for the composer suffix after the final Message heading rather than matching earlier transcript text. The pre-existing signal helper waits for a stopped process before CONT.
